message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file noise complaints through the city’s official channels. The City of Atlanta’s **Department of Public Safety** (or the local police department) handles most noise‑related violations under the city’s noise ordinance.

### How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Where to Go |
|------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Gather Information** | Note the time, location, and nature of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). |
| 2 | **Call 311** | Dial **311** from any Atlanta phone (or 911 for emergencies). The dispatcher will connect you to the appropriate department. |
| 3 | **Use the Online Portal** | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website and navigate to the “Noise Complaint” section. You can submit a form online. |
| 4 | **Visit the Police Station** | If you prefer in person, go to the nearest police precinct and speak with an officer. |
| 5 | **Follow Up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any follow‑up questions. |

### Contact Details

| Department | Phone | Email | Website |
|------------|-------|-------|---------|
| City of Atlanta – Department of Public Safety | 404‑656‑4000 | publicsafety@cityofatlanta.org | https://www.atlantaga.gov/public-safety |
| Atlanta Police Department | 404‑656‑4000 | police@cityofatlanta.org | https://www.atlantaga.gov/police |
| 311 Service | 311 (from within Atlanta) | 311@cityofatlanta.org | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 |

### Quick Tips

- **Time Limits:** Noise complaints are usually addressed within 24–48 hours, but the exact response time can vary.
- **Documentation:** If you’re dealing with repeated disturbances, keep a log of dates, times, and descriptions; this helps authorities track patterns.
- **Legal Basis:** Atlanta’s noise ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 3 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets permissible decibel limits and quiet hours (typically 10 p.m.–7 a.m.).

If you’re unsure whether your situation qualifies as a noise violation, you can always call 311 first—they’ll guide you to the right department.
